'''Rosemary Helen Lowe-McConnell''' (née '''Rosemary Helen Lowe'''; 24 June 1921 – 22 December 2014)<ref>{{Cite news|title = Rosemary Lowe-McConnell - obituary|url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/11333472/Rosemary-Lowe-McConnell-obituary.html|website = Telegraph.co.uk|access-date = 2016-02-07|date = 2015-01-09}}</ref> was an [[England|English]] [[Ichthyology|ichthyologist]], [[Ecology|ecologist]], and [[Limnology|limnologist]] known for research on [[tilapia]] and [[aquaculture]]. Working in the tropical waters of [[Africa]] and [[South America]], Lowe-McConnell was a pioneer in the study of [[tropical fish]] [[ecology]] and an early adopter of the use of [[scuba diving]] for scientific research.<ref name="Bruton1994">{{cite journal|last = Bruton|first = Michael N.|date = July 30, 1994|title = The life and work of Rosemary Lowe-McConnell: pioneer in tropical fish ecology|journal = Environmental Biology of Fishes|volume = 41|issue = 1–4|pages = 67–80|doi = 10.1007/bf00023803|s2cid = 35408519}}</ref>

==Biography==
Rosemary Helen Lowe was educated at Howell's School in [[Denbigh]], [[Wales]] before receiving B.S., M.Sc., and D.Sc. degrees from the [[University of Liverpool]].<ref name="Haines2001">{{cite book|last=Haines|first=Catharine M. C.|title=International Women in Science: A Biographical Dictionary to 1950|url=https://archive.org/details/internationalwom00hain|url-access=registration|access-date=28 May 2012|year=2001|publisher=ABC-CLIO|isbn=978-1-57607-090-1|pages=[https://archive.org/details/internationalwom00hain/page/183 183]–}}</ref> She went from there to the [[Freshwater Biological Association]], [[Near and Far Sawrey|Far Sawrey]] working on various projects aimed at producing wartime food from fresh waters.<ref name="grauniad"/>

Following [[World War II]], in 1945, Lowe-McConnell conducted a survey of tilapia [[Fishery|fisheries]] in the southern part of [[Lake Malawi|Lake Nyasa]], continuing the previous survey done in 1939 by [[Ethelwynn Trewavas]], Kate Ricardo Bertram, and John Borley. Lowe-McConnell received no support from any fisheries research organisations for this survey and relied heavily on local fishermen for assistance with her research.  As a result of these studies, Lowe-McConnell produced a valuable account of the tilapia fishery that formed a basis for subsequent investigation into Malawian [[cichlid]]s. In the survey, Lowe-McConnell identified five [[Tilapiine cichlid|tilapiine]] species, as well as studied other economically viable fish, including [[Labeo mesops]].<ref name="Bruton1994" />

In 1948, Lowe-McConnell studied as a Research Officer in the British Overseas Research Service on the Ugandan shores of [[Lake Victoria]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title = Rosemary Lowe-McConnell, obituary|journal = Environmental Biology of Fishes|date = 2015-03-21|issn = 0378-1909|pages = 1719–1722|volume = 98|issue = 6|doi = 10.1007/s10641-015-0409-1|language = en|first1 = Melanie L. J.|last1 = Stiassny|first2 = Leslie S.|last2 = Kaufman|doi-access = free| bibcode=2015EnvBF..98.1719S }}</ref> Here, she helped found the East African Fisheries Research Organisation and briefly served as its Acting Director.<ref name="Bruton1994" />  Her research again focused again on tilapia as a potential fisheries species.<ref name=":0" />  During this time, she assisted many researchers, including [[Hugh B. Cott|Hugh Cott]] on his [[crocodile]] studies and [[Humphry Greenwood]] in his research on [[Cichlid|haplochromine cichlids]].<ref name="Bruton1994" />  Lowe-McConnell's research during this period served as a foundation for later assessments of the impact fishing and other human activities have on food fishes.<ref name="Bruton1994" />

After she married the geologist Richard McConnell on 31st of December 1953, she was required to resign from the [[Colonial Service|British Colonial Service]] due to the organization's marriage bar.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="grauniad">{{Cite news|title = Rosemary Lowe-McConnell obituary|url = https://www.theguardian.com/science/2015/jan/29/rosemary-lowe-mcconnell|newspaper = The Guardian|date = 2015-01-29|access-date = 2016-02-07|issn = 0261-3077|language = en-GB|first = Jennifer|last = Greenwood}}</ref>  This rule prevented the permanent employment of a married woman in the British Public Service.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|title = The tilapia trail: the life story of a fish biologist|journal = Neotropical Ichthyology|issn = 1679-6225|pages = 85|volume = 5|issue = 1|doi = 10.1590/S1679-62252007000100013|first = Horácio Ferreira Júlio|last = Júnior|year = 2007|doi-access = free}}</ref>

Soon after their wedding, the McConnells moved to the [[Bechuanaland Protectorate]], where their joint research focused on [[Botswana]]n [[natural history]]. During this time, Lowe-McConnell was appointed as the ichthyologist on the R.V. Cape St Mary to conduct marine fieldwork on the unexplored [[The Guianas|Guiana shelf]].  She also developed her [[Okavango River|Okavango]] fish collection, now housed in the [[Natural History Museum, London]].  In 1955, she described four new species and subspecies of tilapias in [[Lake Jipe]] and the [[Pangani River]].<ref name="Bruton1994" />

In 1957, Richard became director of the Geological Survey in [[British Guiana]] and Lowe-McConnell provided research support.  She was also hired by the Guiana Department of Agriculture and Fisheries to conduct fish surveys in unstudied areas, which provided a foundation for studying the diverse and ecologically complex [[Rupununi]] fish communities.<ref name=":0" />  Her 1959 paper on the differences between tilapia species served as the basis for [[Ethelwynn Trewavas]]' division of tilapiine fish genera.<ref name="Bruton1994" />

When Richard retired in 1962, the McConnells moved back to England, where Lowe-McConnell joined the [[Natural History Museum, London]] as an Associate.  While at the museum, Lowe-McConnell worked closely with [[Ethelwynn Trewavas]]e on their extensive collections and global research.<ref name=":0" />  In 1968, Lowe-McConnell was appointed as ichthyologist on the [[Royal Society|Royal Society of London]]/[[Royal Geographical Society]] Xavantina Cachimbo Expedition to northeastern [[Mato Grosso]], [[Brazil]].<ref name="Bruton1994" />  She traveled to Gatun Lake in Panamá in 1979 to assist Thomas Zaret in studying the impact of an introduced [[cichla]] species.<ref name=":1" />

Lowe-McConnell was widely known as a leader in her field and engaged with numerous international conferences, projects, and publications.<ref name=":0" />  Her work was requested by global organizations, including the [[Food and Agriculture Organization]], [[United Nations Development Programme]], and the International Center of Living Aquatic Resources Management.  During the 1980s through the early 2000s, Lowe-McConnell worked with Great Lakes research projects and governance bodies, including the [[Lake Victoria Fisheries Organization]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1997, Lowe-McConnell was awarded the [[Linnean Medal]] of Zoology by the [[Linnean Society of London]].<ref name="nndb.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.nndb.com/honors/036/000111700/|title=Linnean Medal|publisher=NNDB|access-date=29 May 2012}}</ref>

Lowe-McConnell continued to remain active in her field until her death on 22 December 2014 at St. George’s Park in [[Ditchling]], England.<ref name=":0" />

==Legacy==
The Pike Cichlid, ''[[Crenicichla rosemariae]]'' <small>[[Sven Oscar Kullander|S. O. Kullander]], 1997</small> is named after her.<ref name = ETYFish>{{cite web | url = http://www.etyfish.org/cichlidae6/ | title = Order Order CICHLIFORMES: Family CICHLIDAE: Subfamily CICHLINAE (a-c) | access-date= 12 November 2021 | author1 = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J. Lazara | name-list-style = amp | work = The ETYFish Project Fish Name Etymology Database | publisher = Christopher Scharpf and Kenneth J. Lazara | date = 22 September 2018}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
Lowe-McConnell was authored or co-author for over 80 publications and edited or co-edited three books.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|title = Lifetime list of publications by Rosemary Lowe-McConnell|journal = Environmental Biology of Fishes|date = 1994-11-01|issn = 0378-1909|pages = 81–83|volume = 41|issue = 1–4|doi = 10.1007/BF00023804|language = en|first = Michael N.|last = Bruton|s2cid = 40082424}}</ref>
* ''Notes on the fishes found in Georgetown fish markets and their seasonal fluctuations'' (1962)
* ''Man-made Lakes'' (1966)
* ''Speciation in tropical environments'', with [[Ernst Mayr]] (1969)
* ''Fish communities in tropical freshwaters: their distribution, ecology and evolution'' (1975)
* ''Ecology of fishes in tropical waters'' (1977)
* ''The functioning of freshwater ecosystems'', with E. D. Le Cren (1980)
* ''Ecological studies in tropical fish communities'' (1987)
* ''Symposium on Resource Use and Conservation of the African Great Lakes: Bujumbura 1989; with 18 tables'' (1992)
* ''Land of waters: explorations in the natural history of Guyana, South America'' (2000)
* ''Recent research in the African great lakes: fisheries, biodiversity and cichild evolution'' (2003)
* ''The Tilapia Trail: The life story of a fish biologist'' (2006)
